answer: Think of it like this: every agent’s receipt must be signed at a unique vertex in a dynamic graph. The violet pigment used to mark the vertex dries at a fixed rate, so fakes must wait 0.9s for their pigment to bind before submitting. Worse, the vertex map shifts after each signature, forcing farms to recompute the path for every single identity. Each extra head adds 0.9s of rigidity—no bulk sauce can cheat the drying time.
